Ava (People Ops): Heads-up — we have a bunch of questions about the Q2 offsite travel & expense rules. Can we confirm per diem, receipts, and booking rules so I can update the quick guide?
Diego (Sales): Quick question — is there a hotel rate cap for non-enterprise events or should we just book business standard?
Maya (Eng): Also: meal receipts. Does Finance require receipts for every meal or do we use per diem? I remember something about domestic vs international.
Ben (Finance): TL;DR: domestic day-per-diems and receipts rules below. Long version: see details.
Ben (Finance): Domestic travel: we reimburse actual meals up to receipts OR you can use daily per diem of $75 (meals only) if you’re away overnight. International per diem varies by country — submit country code and we’ll apply rates.
Ben (Finance): Hotel: guideline caps — $250/night domestic metro, $350/night high-cost city (NYC/SF/LON). If you need to exceed cap, get manager pre-approval + note reason in the expense note. No surprises after the fact.
Ava (People Ops): Good — can we codify the pre-approval flow? I’m thinking: manager approval in TravelPerk + a short justification in the expense submission.
Ben (Finance): Exactly. If booking on corporate card (p-card/TravelPerk), manager auto-notified. If personal booking for reimbursement, attach manager's approval email or Slack message.
Maya (Eng): For receipts threshold — what about coffee/snacks under $25? Do we need receipts?
Ben (Finance): Receipts required for any single expense >= $25. Anything under $25: log it as "misc" in the expense form with amount and brief note; no receipt required. Exceptions if merchant requires a receipt for reimbursement.
Diego (Sales): What about rideshares vs car rental vs mileage?
Ben (Finance): Rideshare: submit receipt. Rental car: receipt + fuel. Mileage: use our mileage form in Expensify (or the odometer snapshot) and mileage rate is current IRS rate — check the header link in the Travel policy.
TravelBot: Automated reminder: all expenses must be submitted within 60 days of trip end date. Late submissions may be declined except with People Ops/Finance exception. Link to guide: https://redwood.example/internal/travel-policy
Ava (People Ops): Quick checklist I'm adding to the guide (please ack): 1) Book via TravelPerk when possible 2) Use p-card for hotel/air when available 3) Pre-approval for >cap or international 4) Receipts for >=$25 5) Per diem $75 domestic or actual receipts 6) Submit within 60 days 7) Manager + Finance approvals required
Maya (Eng): Ack, and add: if the trip is <12 hours and no overnight, meals are not eligible for per diem.
Ben (Finance): Good call — add that. Also: if you choose per diem for meals, you can't also submit meal receipts for the same day.
Ava (People Ops): Note for interns/temporary contractors: they follow same reimbursement policy, but any international travel needs People Ops sign-off before booking.
Diego (Sales): One more — conference registration fees?
Ben (Finance): Conference fees: expense under "Conference" with receipt. If refundable, indicate refund policy and coordinate with Finance before paying.
Ava (People Ops): I'll update the one-pager and post it to the travel policy doc. Will ping this thread once live. :rocket:
Diego (Sales): Thanks!
Maya (Eng): Nice, thanks all.
Ben (Finance): If anyone wants the small JSON snippet we use to import expenses into the ledger, DM me.
Ava (People Ops): For the guide, I'll paste the minimal expense form example here for devs who script uploads:
Ava (People Ops): ```
{
  "date": "2025-05-12",
  "category": "hotel",
  "amount": "312.50",
  "currency": "USD",
  "merchant": "Hotel Example",
  "receipt_attached": "true",
  "manager_approval": "diego@example.com",
  "notes": "offsite - pre-approved"
}
```
TravelBot: Reminder set — People Ops will be pinged to publish the updated quick guide at 1719805400.
Ava (People Ops): Thanks everyone — I'll publish by EOD and add a short FAQ for edge cases.
Diego (Sales): :thumbsup:
Maya (Eng): :+1:
Ben (Finance): Closing loop: Finance will review edge-case exceptions within 5 business days of submission.
